Subject: Clarify billing for long sessions and rounding/minimums

Rafael / Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — AcmeHealth Product & Procurement teams reviewed the cost examples and we still have a few open questions before we can sign: how do you handle multi-hour conversations that exceed our typical context sizes? Specifically:

- If a single user session accumulates 120k+ tokens across the day, how is that aggregated for billing?
- Do you charge per "call" or do you roll up tokens into a conversation window?
- What rounding rules and minimums apply (per-call minimum, per-day minimums, or per-session floors)?

I've attached our proposed SLA excerpt for reference (acme-proposed-SLA.pdf). If you can provide one or two simple invoice examples with numbers we can circulate to procurement, that would help.

Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise explanation and two worked examples; I've also attached a sample invoice spreadsheet (sample-invoice-aggregation.xlsx) that walks the math. High level summary up front: we bill tokens at the request level, but we perform deterministic aggregation and credits for KV/prefix reuse within a bounded session window; rounding and minimums depend on the SKU.

Key points (short):
- Per-request accounting: every API call is tokenized and initially counted at the call level.
- Billing buckets: tokens are grouped into billing buckets specific to the SKU (standard = 8,000-token bucket).
- Minimum billable per call: standard SKU has a 1,000-token per-call minimum (streams treated as calls every 30s by default).
- Conversation rollup: we apply a 10-minute conversation rollup window for KV/prefix reuse credits — repeated prefixes within that window get a reuse credit (see example 2).
- Rounding: we round up to the nearest 100 tokens after aggregation and credits are applied; then buckets are applied.

Example A — single long generation (one-shot large prompt)
- Raw tokens produced: 120,400
- No KV reuse because single generation; rounding up to nearest 100 -> 120,400 (already multiple of 100)
- Bucket size 8,000 -> ceil(120,400 / 8,000) = 16 buckets billed
- Per-bucket rate = $X (see spreadsheet) -> invoice line shows 16 * rate.

Example B — multi-turn chat with prefix reuse across 6 hours (user re-uses same context frequently)
- Summed raw tokens across calls: 180,250
- We identify repeated prefixes within 10-minute rollup windows and apply a 50% reuse credit to those prefix tokens (this is conservative; real credit depends on exact overlap)
- Post-credit tokens: 150,600 -> round up to 150,600 -> buckets = ceil(150,600 / 8,000) = 19 buckets billed
- Streaming sessions: if the client streams continuously for >30s, we treat each 30s slice as a new call (but identical prefixes in ≤10 minutes get reuse credit).

Pilot concession note: for pilot customers we can apply a 'minimum waiver' for first 90 days (see Vanessa's email for specifics).

I realize this is a lot of detail — the spreadsheet contains line-by-line invoice mockups for both examples (pro-rated monthly view as well). If you'd like, we can convert one of these into a single-page appendix for your procurement team.

Rafael Mendes

Rafael / Priyom — quick internal note on commercial flexibility for ACME-4821. Procurement is price-sensitive and the clinical-summation use case will look worst-case on the 30s stream-slicing math. Proposed commercial package we can offer to close pilot quickly: 

- 90-day minimum-waiver: waive the per-call minimums for first 90 days of the pilot (they still incur per-bucket charges but we won't enforce the per-call floor).
- 25% pilot discount on per-bucket rates for the first 3 billing cycles.
- Monthly overage cap during pilot: we cap customer liability to 120% of the forecasted monthly burn (forecast in the spreadsheet). Any excess month => credits applied next invoice.
- Contract language snippet (suggested) to include in SOW: "Redwood will apply conversation rollup and prefix-reuse credits as described; for the pilot period, Redwood will waive per-call minimums and apply a 25% discount to per-bucket rates. Billing disputes related to aggregation must be raised within 30 days of invoice."

I've attached the sample-invoice-aggregation.xlsx with the capped/invoice view. Rafael — if you agree, send Sarah a single-page SOW paragraph and cc Priyom.

"Redwood will bill tokens using per-request accounting with deterministic aggregation into billing buckets. Customer liability during the pilot is capped at 120% of forecasted monthly burn; any overage above that cap will be issued as a credit to the customer's subsequent invoice."
